subject: science

concepts.title: Force - A Push or Pull
concepts.definition: An external influence as a push or pull that can change an object's state of motion, speed, direction, or shape.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: A force is fundamentally a push or a pull acting on an object.
question_patterns: what is a force
identify actions as push or pull
how does a force affect an object

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the action involves pushing (moving away) or pulling (drawing closer).

concepts.title: Forces due to Interaction
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, in brief, the mutual action between at least two bodies that gives a force acting on each of them.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: A force cannot exist in isolation; it requires interaction between two or more objects.
question_patterns: why does a force require interaction
explain how interaction leads to a force
what is needed for a force to come into play

solution_steps.explain: Determine the two objects that are interacting to produce the force.

concepts.title: Net Force in Same Direction
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, the total force acting on an object when multiple forces are applied along the exact same line of action and direction, calculated by summing their magnitudes.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Forces acting in the common direction combine by addition.
question_patterns: calculate the net force when two forces act in the same direction
find the total force if two people push a box in the same direction
what is the resultant force of forces acting together in the same direction

solution_steps.explain: Since the forces act in the same direction, they reinforce each other.

concepts.title: Net Force in Opposite Directions
concepts.definition: The resultant force acting on an object when two forces are applied in directly opposing directions, calculated as the absolute difference between their magnitudes.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Forces acting in opposite directions oppose each other and subtract.
question_patterns: find the net force when two forces act in opposite directions
calculate the resultant force of opposing forces
what is the net force on a rope pulled in opposite directions

solution_steps.action: Find the absolute difference between the forces
solution_steps.explain: Opposing forces cancel each other out partially, so we subtract the smaller from the larger.

concepts.title: Muscular Force
concepts.definition: In brief, the contact force applied by the action of muscles inside a living body.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Internal muscles exert forces to perform physical tasks like lifting, pushing, or breathing.
question_patterns: what is muscular force
give examples of muscular force in animals
is muscular force a contact force

solution_steps.explain: Verify if the force originates from the contraction or expansion of muscles in a living organism.

concepts.title: Force of Friction
concepts.definition: A resistive contact force that acts between surfaces touching to oppose their relative motion.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Friction always acts opposite to the direction of motion to slow things down.
question_patterns: what is friction
why does a rolling ball stop
in which direction does friction act

solution_steps.action: Identify relative motion and surface contact
solution_steps.explain: Friction arises when two surfaces slide or attempt to slide past each other.

concepts.title: Electrostatic Force
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the non-contact force applied by a charged body on another charged or uncharged body.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Charges can attract or repel each other from a distance without physical contact.
question_patterns: what is electrostatic force
explain why a rubbed straw attracts another straw
is electrostatic force a contact force

solution_steps.explain: Verify if the force is caused by electric charges acquired through friction or other means.

concepts.title: Gravitational Force
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, the attractive non-contact force that pulls objects toward each other, most noticeably pulling objects toward the Earth's center.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Every object in the universe exerts an attractive pull on every other object.
question_patterns: what is gravity
why do leaves fall to the ground
is gravitational force attractive or repulsive

solution_steps.explain: Gravity is the universal attractive force acting between any two masses.

concepts.title: Pressure
concepts.definition: The amount of perpendicular force distributed over a unit surface area.
concepts.key_idea: Pressure varies in inverse proportion with the area over which a force is indeed applied.
question_patterns: calculate the pressure exerted on a surface
find the pressure given force and area
what is the pressure if a force is applied over an area

solution_steps.explain: Pressure is defined as force per unit area.

concepts.title: Pressure Exerted by Liquids
concepts.definition: In brief, the pressure applied by a fluid on the both bottom and walls of its container, which increases with the liquid's depth column.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Liquids exert pressure in all directions, and this pressure is equal at the same depth.
question_patterns: does liquid exert pressure on walls
how does liquid pressure vary with depth
why does a rubber sheet bulge when water is poured

solution_steps.explain: Liquid pressure depends on depth and acts perpendicular to the container walls.

concepts.title: Atmospheric Pressure
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the pressure applied by the air's weight column in the Earth's atmosphere on a unit area.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: The massive weight of air above us exerts a huge pressure, which is balanced by our internal body pressure.
question_patterns: what is atmospheric pressure
why are we not crushed by atmospheric pressure
how does a rubber sucker stick to a wall

solution_steps.explain: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the gravitational pull on the air column extending above the surface.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Two friends push a heavy box in the same direction. One applies a force of {force_a} N and the other applies {force_b} N. What is the net force acting on the box?

extracted_variables.force_a: force applied by the first friend in Newtons
extracted_variables.force_b: force applied by the second friend in Newtons

solution_template.explain: Since the forces act in the same direction, they reinforce each other.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Two teams pull a rope in opposite directions. Team A pulls with a force of {force_a} N and Team B pulls with a force of {force_b} N. What is the net force on the rope?

extracted_variables.force_a: pulling force of Team A in Newtons
extracted_variables.force_b: pulling force of Team B in Newtons

solution_template.action: Find the absolute difference between the forces
solution_template.explain: Opposing forces cancel each other out partially, so we subtract the smaller from the larger.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A force of {force} N is applied perpendicularly on a wooden plank over an area of {area} m^2. Calculate the pressure exerted on the plank.

solution_template.explain: Pressure is defined as force per unit area.

questions: Give two examples each of situations in which you push or pull to change the state of motion of objects.
Give two examples of situations in which applied force causes a change in the shape of an object.

Fill in the blanks in the following statements: (a) To draw water from a well we have to __________ at the rope. (b) A charged body __________ an uncharged body towards it. (c) To move a loaded trolley we have to __________ it. (d) The north pole of a magnet __________ the north pole of another magnet.

An archer stretches her bow while taking aim at the target. She then releases the arrow, which begins to move towards the target. Based on this information fill up the gaps in the following statements using the following terms: muscular, contact, non-contact, gravity, friction, shape, attraction. (a) To stretch the bow, the archer applies a force that causes a change in its __________. (b) The force applied by the archer to stretch the bow is an example of __________ force. (c) The type of force responsible for a change in the state of motion of the arrow is an example of a __________ force. (d) While the arrow moves towards its target, the forces acting on it are due to __________ and that due to __________ of air.

In the following situations identify the agent exerting the force and the object on which it acts. State the effect of the force in each case: (a) Squeezing a piece of lemon between the fingers to extract its juice. (b) Taking out paste from a toothpaste tube. (c) A load suspended from a spring while its other end is on a hook fixed to a wall. (d) An athlete making a high jump to clear the bar at a certain height.
A blacksmith hammers a hot piece of iron while making a tool. How does the force due to hammering affect the piece of iron?

An inflated balloon was pressed against a wall after it has been rubbed with a piece of synthetic cloth. It was found that the balloon sticks to the wall. What force might be responsible for the attraction between the balloon and the wall?
Name the forces acting on a plastic bucket containing water held above ground level in your hand. Discuss why the forces acting on the bucket do not bring a change in its state of motion.
A rocket has been fired upwards to launch a satellite in its orbit. Name the two forces acting on the rocket immediately after leaving the launching pad.

When we press the bulb of a dropper with its nozzle kept in water, air in the dropper is seen to escape in the form of bubbles. Once we release the pressure on the bulb, water gets filled in the dropper. The rise of water in the dropper is due to: (a) pressure of water, (b) gravity of the earth, (c) shape of rubber bulb, (d) atmospheric pressure.
